images.title: A coil times a heel is a lotus
images.purpose: Shows that multiplying two Egyptian landmarks, 100 × 10, gives another landmark, 1000.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One row: a coil, a times sign, a heel, an equals sign and a lotus, each large, with its value under it.
images.exact_structure: Left to right, evenly spaced and large: one coil symbol (teal #0072B2), a dark times sign, one heel symbol (upside down U, teal), a dark equals sign, one lotus symbol (reddish purple #CC79A7). Under the coil 100, under the heel 10, under the lotus 1000. Exactly 3 symbols and 2 signs. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: In a base, a landmark times a landmark is another landmark.
images.description: Shows that multiplying two Egyptian landmarks, 100 × 10, gives another landmark, 1000.
images.context: Worked example: 100 × 10 = 1000; also holds in base 5 (25 × 125 = 3125).

image_decisions.why: Three symbols in one line make the landmark product property immediate.
